pool.text: Sir Arthur Chichester undertook the Plantation of Belfast and surrounding area.
Newcomers were temporarily expelled by an English Parliamentarian army after being denounced.
Anglicans favored the older Royal Belfast Academy established in this year.
The Belfast Fever Hospital began as the first of successive institutions for a hospital.
The Society organised a republican insurrection in hopes of French assistance.
Anglican establishment disaffection contributed to the union with Great Britain.
The Orange Order organized an event that became a public holiday.
Parliament opening at Stormont was overshadowed by unemployed protests.
Short & Harland Ltd began the manufacture of aircraft in the docks area.
Nearly a third of industrial workers were unemployed and malnourished.
The German Luftwaffe appeared four times over the city.
The British Army committed to the longest continuous deployment.
International Workers Day has been recognized as a public holiday since this year.
The British government sold the nationalised company to the Canadian company Bombardier.
Belfast hosted its very first gay pride event during this year.
The port received its first cruise ship, bringing an entirely new phenomenon.
Unionists lost overall control of Belfast City Council.
Alban Maginness became the first nationalist Lord Mayor of Belfast from the SDLP.
The Good Friday Belfast Agreement returned a power-sharing assembly.
Work began to transform former shipyard land into a waterfront development.
